subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput follow-up
messages:

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated for real-time scoring?

Thanks for the call today, Marissa. Quick recap and a couple of clarifications from our side: we need to do real-time scoring for our streaming pipeline. Target SLO is p95 latency <= 100ms for single-turn prompts (most calls are ~200 tokens). Steady-state throughput will be ~200 req/s, with predictable spikes up to ~1,000 req/s during peak batch windows.

A few asks:
- Can Redwood hit the 100ms p95 under that profile on Hosted API, or would Dedicated be required?
- If Dedicated, what ballpark capacity do you recommend (GPUs / nodes)?
- We also need to understand cold-start behavior and instance warmup for models with caching.

Also note: we'll need a SOC 2 checklist for procurement, but that's a separate thread.

Appreciate a short summary and next steps.

Alex
Director of Engineering
QuantAnalytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-03-01T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated for real-time scoring?

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and for sharing the throughput numbers. Short answers up-front:

- Hosted API: great for rapid onboarding and variable workloads; for strict p95 <= 100ms at sustained 200 req/s with spikes to 1k req/s, Hosted may struggle to guarantee that SLA because of multi-tenant variability and cold-starts. Best-effort latency is often very good, but you won't get the same predictability as Dedicated.

- Dedicated capacity: recommended when you need predictable tail latency and capacity guarantees. Based on the profile you shared, a Dedicated pool sized for consistent 200 req/s with headroom for bursts will give you the controls (reserved GPUs, isolated queues, warm workers, prefix/KV cache) to hit p95 targets.

Next steps I propose:
1) Tech deep-dive with Rishi (our infra SRE/SE) to validate model characteristics and map to instance sizing.
2) I can send a 1-page ballpark capacity & cost worksheet (attached) with a couple of configuration options (conservative / optimized).
3) If you want to evaluate Hosted first, we can spin up a short pilot and measure real latency under your traffic pattern.

I've attached a short PDF that outlines Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoffs and a ballpark spreadsheet (attachment) — see QuantAnalytics-ballpark-capacity.xlsx and redwood-deploy-options.pdf.

Would you like me to schedule the tech deep-dive for early next week? Rishi is available Tuesday/Wednesday AM PT.

Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated for real-time scoring? — infra recommendations

Alex — following up with some concrete sizing guidance after looking at the numbers Marissa sent and our perf baselines. A few assumptions: single-turn prompts ~200 tokens, model family comparable to open-medium/large encoder-decoder style (latency characteristics similar to 13B-class), and we assume use of prefix/KV caching for multi-message flows where applicable.

Option A — Dedicated (recommended for your SLO):
- Baseline pool: 4 x high-memory accelerator nodes (equivalent to H100-class), each node configured with 32 concurrent long-lived workers and aggressive KV caching.
- Expected steady-state: ~50 req/s per node with p95 latency ~60–90ms (depends on exact model); pool of 4 yields ~200 req/s steady with buffer for losses/failover.
- Burst handling: enable autoscale burst to add 2 nodes (soft limit) to absorb ~1k req/s short spikes; queuing/routing policies keep p95 within target for high-priority routes.
- Benefits: deterministic tail latency, pre-warmed kernels, dedicated GPU memory for KV caches.

Option B — Hosted (pilot / short eval):
- Quick path to get data: run a 1-week pilot with traffic replay (we can set up a small prod-like load) to measure p95 under your exact patterns. Good if you want to compare cost & perf before committing to Dedicated.

Operational notes:
- Cold-starts: with Dedicated you'll avoid cold-starts for the main worker pool; Hosted can rewarm but may have variance.
- Observability: we'll provide per-route latency dashboards and token-level breakdowns so you can correlate spikes to model/memory behavior.

If this sounds right, Marissa — I can convert Option A into a short technical proposal (node configuration, estimated monthly commit) and a rollout plan (canary -> full rollout) for your procurement team.

Alex — ping me with a couple of times and I'll block Rishi + infra SME for the deep dive.

Thanks,
